claim: This leaf's OWN state/cost addition (the scene-B insert bus wiring, the bins1->bins2 schedule, the gating/lifecycle control state, plus its synthetic per-slot occupant kernel) -- NOT the ext-mem footprint of whichever concrete Surge FX algorithm actually occupies bins1/bins2 in a real preset, which is that algorithm leaf's own SXT-015/016 accounting.

external_writable_memory.note: the synthetic occupant kernel (BiquadInstance) is register-only (on-chip); it touches no external buffer. A concrete tail-bearing occupant (Delay/Reverb1/Reverb2/Chorus/etc.) landed in bins1 or bins2 owns its own external-memory accounting separately, and its long buffers must live in external WRITABLE memory -- never flash (AGENTS.md).

external_traffic.note: no external-memory transactions originate from this leaf's own routing/scheduling/lifecycle logic or its synthetic occupant

on_chip_small_state.note: two instances (bins1, bins2) = 2 x 321 bits + 21 shared routing/lifecycle control bits = 663 bits on-chip total for this leaf's own contribution

ext_mem_traffic_estimate: [PENDING-SXT-016] this leaf's own contribution is 0 words/sample (see external_traffic above); the AGGREGATE estimate for a concrete preset also depends on whichever algorithm leaf's occupant actually lands in bins1/bins2 (e.g. EQ+Chorus for Novuo.fxp, Reverb 2 for Shore.fxp), which is out of this leaf's scope -- no aggregate number is invented here
long_buffers_policy: delay/reverb-class buffers live in external WRITABLE memory; processing stays on-chip; flash is not writable delay memory (AGENTS.md) -- not applicable to this leaf's own (register-only) contribution
scene_bus_note: this leaf accounts for ONE scene's insert bus (scene B). The scene-A insert bus (rf-ains*), the send buses (rf-send*) and the global bus (rf-global*, landed as rf-rf-global2) each carry their own instances and their own accounting; nothing here is a per-patch total.
